title: NeuroPriv: Adversarial Representation Learning for Privacy in Wearable EEG Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.00390v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Wearable EEG systems may expose sensitive information beyond their intended health function, creating substantial risks to neuroprivacy. In this work, we show that commonly used EEG features can reveal participant identity and demographic attributes in addition to supporting the intended cognitive task. Wearable EEG is increasingly being explored for cognitive monitoring, neurological assessment, and longitudinal digital-health applications, yet many systems assume that transmitting compact spectral or spatial features instead of raw EEG provides sufficient privacy protection. Using EEGMAT as a motivating case study, we find that compact EEG features achieve a balanced accuracy of 0.788 for cognitive-state classification while enabling gender, age, and subject-identity inference with balanced accuracies of 0.858, 0.789, and 0.692, respectively. We further show that privacy-aware representation learning preserves task performance at 0.7

translated_title: NeuroPriv：面向可穿戴脑电图系统隐私的对抗表征学习
translated_abstract: 可穿戴脑电图系统可能会暴露超出其预期健康功能的敏感信息，对神经隐私构成重大风险。在这项工作中，我们表明常用的脑电图特征除了支持预期的认知任务之外，还能泄露参与者的身份和人口统计学属性。可穿戴脑电图正日益被探索用于认知监测、神经评估和纵向数字健康应用，然而许多系统假设传输紧凑的频谱或空间特征而非原始脑电信号即可提供充分的隐私保护。以EEGMAT作为动机案例研究，我们发现紧凑的脑电图特征在认知状态分类上达到0.788的平衡准确率，同时还能推断性别、年龄和受试者身份，其平衡准确率分别为0.858、0.789和0.692。我们进一步表明，隐私感知的表征学习能够在保持任务性能于0.7……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文揭示紧凑脑电图特征可被用于推断性别、年龄与身份等敏感信息，并提出基于对抗表征学习的NeuroPriv方法，在保持认知任务性能的同时保护可穿戴脑电图系统的神经隐私。
en_tdlr: NeuroPriv leverages adversarial representation learning to protect privacy in wearable EEG systems, preventing inference of sensitive attributes such as gender, age, and identity from compact EEG features while preserving cognitive-task performance.
